critical_steps: M_B M_B^*=|B|I_4 is equivalent to six vanishing character sums of differences.
For a prime p, each zero character sum has uniform residue histogram; thus p divides |B|, while rank forces |B|≥4.
For p=2 both parity planes realize the bound and Fourier inversion proves uniqueness.
For p=3 six explicitly balanced frequencies attain the bound, and two independent exact enumerations show all 27 optimal frequency subsets form the translation orbit.
For p≥5 a line with direction (1,2,3) has nonzero pairing with all six relevant differences and attains size p.
integrity.exact_domain: The four-point affine simplex {0,e1,e2,e3} in the three-dimensional vector space over every prime field; character-frequency subsets in the same dual vector space.
integrity.proof_basis: Prime cyclotomic divisibility, rank, explicit balanced-projection constructions, binary Fourier inversion, exhaustive ternary integer checker.
integrity.unproved_limits: No classification is given of every optimum for p≥5, or of weighted/multiset frequency designs.

limitations: Distinct unweighted frequency sets only; arbitrary weights and repetitions excluded.
For primes at least five, only one minimizing construction is claimed, not a full classification.
The ternary cardinality and orbit are certified by a complete, small, exact-integer census, while the all-prime cutoff has a symbolic proof.

title: Prime-field simplex tight sampling has a unique ternary optimizer orbit
